articles.title: Postal Votes Can Be Hand Delivered to Polling Stations Today
articles.excerpt: Voters in Heywood, Middleton, and Rochdale can hand deliver their postal votes to polling stations before 10pm today, 30 July.
articles.content_html:
A postal vote can be hand delivered to any polling station in Heywood, Middleton, Pennines, and Rochdale before 10pm today, Thursday 30 July.

Voters who have not returned their postal votes are advised to complete a Postal Vote Return Form when delivering their ballot.

This option is available to ensure that those who may have forgotten to send their postal votes can still participate in the election process.

Polling stations will remain open until the deadline, allowing voters to ensure their votes are counted.

articles.title: Greater Manchester Holds Largest By-Election in UK History
articles.excerpt: Voters across Greater Manchester, including Rochdale, are participating in the largest by-election in UK history today, with calls to support Labour candidate Bev Craig for the City Region Mayor position.
articles.content_html:
Today, Greater Manchester is witnessing the largest by-election in UK history, with voters from Bolton, Bury, Oldham, Rochdale, Salford, Tameside, Trafford, Stockport, Wigan, and Manchester taking part.

The by-election is significant as it aims to elect a new City Region Mayor, with Labour candidate Bev Craig receiving endorsements from various local leaders and organisations.

Polling stations are open throughout the day, and residents are encouraged to make their voices heard in this pivotal election.

This event marks a crucial moment for local politics, as the outcome could shape the future direction of the Greater Manchester region.

articles.title: Voters Urged to Support Marlon West in Greater Manchester Election
articles.excerpt: Residents of Greater Manchester are encouraged to vote for Marlon West and the Restore Britain party today, aiming to reclaim control over the region.
articles.content_html:
A call to action has been issued to voters across Greater Manchester to support Marlon West and the Restore Britain party in today's election. The campaign emphasises the importance of unity across the region, including Rochdale, Tameside, and Oldham.

Marlon West's platform focuses on restoring local governance and addressing issues that affect all communities within Greater Manchester. The campaign aims to engage residents in the democratic process and encourage participation in shaping the future of the region.

The election is seen as a pivotal moment for Greater Manchester, with the potential to influence local policies and priorities. Voters are urged to consider the implications of their choices on the future governance of their communities.

Polling stations will be open throughout the day, and residents are reminded to check their registration status and voting locations to ensure their voices are heard.

articles.title: Hopwood Triangle Traffic Trial to Continue Pending Township Vote
articles.excerpt: The Hopwood Triangle traffic calming trial will remain in place until a formal vote by the Heywood Township, following widespread criticism from residents and motorists.
articles.content_html:
A traffic calming trial at the Hopwood Triangle in Heywood will continue pending a formal vote by the Heywood Township. Rochdale Council announced that the scheme, which has faced significant criticism since its introduction, cannot be removed until the township holds a meeting to vote on its future.

The trial introduced several changes to the roads around the Hopwood Triangle, including the closure of Middleton Road at its junction with Manchester Road near St John's Church. This measure was implemented to prevent drivers from using the route as a shortcut. Additionally, Magdala Street has been made one way towards Manchester Road, and new parking restrictions for heavy goods vehicles (HGVs) along with a 20mph speed limit have been established on surrounding residential roads.

North Heywood councillor Bev Place expressed her disappointment that the trial could not be ended immediately, as she had hoped. She stated that highways officers informed her of the need for a township meeting to formally vote on the matter. Councillor Place is working to arrange an extraordinary meeting, as the next scheduled meeting is not until 22nd September. She encouraged residents to share their views directly with Rochdale Council's highways team, noting that she has received numerous objections that must be submitted via email to be formally considered.

A spokesperson for Rochdale Council confirmed that there is no set date for the removal of the traffic restrictions and that they are in discussions with contractors regarding the timeline. The council also mentioned that traffic modelling is not typically conducted for residential side street schemes, and that a live trial is deemed the most effective method for assessing the impact on traffic levels and road safety.
